text:
Maya: Heads-up: seeing hot tenants bounce between prefetch and soft-evict causing extra IO. Brainstorming a "leaseback" micro-lease on demote: keep metadata + a reclaim token for a tiny window so the client can reattach cheaply. Feels lower-risk than a full pin. Opinions? :thought_balloon:

Vikram: The concept makes sense. Two questions: (1) how do we guarantee we don't serve stale reads if a write happened? (2) how does this interact with handoff/ownership?

Maya: For correctness I want to require an epoch/version check on reclaim. Reclaim only allowed if cached epoch == cluster-committed epoch. If mismatch, reclaim rejects and client does normal prefetch. So we don't change consistency model, just optimize happy-path reattach.

Sam: Right but races are tricky. If node A demotes and offers a token, then node B acquires ownership write->epoch++, A tries to reclaim briefly after and gets stale. A must be able to detect that and not serve stale. Epoch check covers that but we also need atomicity for token steal scenarios.

Aisha: Suggest small design rules: 1) leaseback is read-only only (no writes). 2) token is CASed on prefix descriptor; reclaim is CAS+epoch-check. 3) short default window (1s) and per-tenant limit (e.g., 2 reclaims/sec). Example config: `leaseback.window_ms=1000, leaseback.max_reclaims=2`

Vikram: Implementation note: add per-shard reclaim_budget counter that decays over time to avoid stampedes. Also expose metrics: `kv.leaseback.requests`, `kv.leaseback.success`, `kv.leaseback.stale_rejects`, `kv.leaseback.cas_conflicts`.

Maya: Good. For races between reclaimers we do CAS on the token field; losers get `RECLAIM_LOST` and should either trigger async prefetch or return `E_RECLAIM_NEEDED` to caller. Don't block critical read flows on reclaim success.

Sam: Client API: we should return a tri-state: `served_from_leaseback`, `need_prefetch_sync`, `prefer_background_prefetch`. Clients can then decide to block or degrade. Add example: `GET /prefix?leaseback=yes` -> 200+header `X-Cache-Reclaim: leaseback` or 202 `X-Cache-Reclaim: prefetch`

Aisha: Edge cases: tenant-level flags `strict_consistency` should disable leaseback. Also skip on write-heavy prefixes (we can track write-rate moving average).

Vikram: Tests: unit CAS+epoch, integration with handoff (simulate ownership change during reclaim), and chaos that kills node after token claim. Rollout: feature flag default off, staged canary 0.5% then 5% then 100% if metrics stable.

Maya: Rollout plan sounds good. I'll own the RFC with invariants and test plan. Action items: @Vikram prototype token CAS + metrics, @Sam update client error codes and sample client behavior, @Aisha add tenant knobs and write-rate gating. I'll open a small PR for a `read-only` reclaim path this week.
